change_summary: The PLOS ONE editors retracted the article because it was identified as one of a series of submissions with concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process. The editors say these concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. The notice is titled as a retraction of this paper's title, and says the author either did not respond directly or could not be reached.
evaluation: In Section 3 your draft cites Dutta [14] for LURL's 97.4% and 96.8% accuracy and says it chose an LSTM on the strength of these results, which the stored paper reports. In Section 4 your draft starts from the LURL settings reported by Dutta [14] (two LSTM layers, hidden size 650, learning rate 1.0 with decay 0.73, at most 7 epochs), and the stored paper's Table 2 lists these LURL settings. The editors retracted the article because of concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process, and the notice says these concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. Both uses, the model choice in Section 3 and the starting settings in Section 4, rely on this retracted paper, so the impact on your draft is high.
recommendation: The editors retracted the article because of concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process, and they say these concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. In Section 3 the draft says it chose an LSTM on the strength of LURL's 97.4% and 96.8% accuracy results from Dutta [14]. In Section 4 the draft starts from the LURL settings reported by Dutta [14]: two LSTM layers, hidden size 650, learning rate 1.0 with decay 0.73, and at most 7 learning-rate epochs. Raise this with your co-authors or supervisor, replace the Section 3 evidence, and validate the Section 4 settings independently before building on them.
